# When Does Aircraft Registration Expire? The 7-Year Rule
Aircraft registration certificates issued by the FAA expire seven years after the last day of the month in which they were issued. A certificate issued on August 15, 2025, for example, would expire on August 31, 2032. The seven-year duration replaced the old three-year cycle and took effect on January 23, 2023, applying to both new registrations and existing certificates that were valid on that date.
## How the Seven-Year Expiration Works
Under 14 CFR § 47.40, every Certificate of Aircraft Registration expires seven years from the last day of the month of issuance.^1 eCFR. 14 CFR 47.40 – Registration Expiration and Renewal The clock starts at the end of the month, not on the exact issue date, so a certificate issued on March 3 and one issued on March 28 both expire on March 31 seven years later.
## How to Renew Before Expiration
Renewal opens six months before the expiration date. The FAA mails a renewal notice to the address on file with instructions and a security code that allows online submission.^5 Federal Aviation Administration. Re-Registration and Renewal of Aircraft Registration The notice identifies the expiration date and the three-month “timely filing window” (roughly months five, four, and three before expiration) designed to give the FAA enough processing time to issue the new certificate before the old one runs out.

    FAA ISSUES NEW AIRCRAFT RE-REGISTRATION AND RENEWAL OF AIRCRAFT REGISTRATION RULES  

 The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has published new regulations that dramatically alter the aircraft registration process and establish new requirements to ensure registration records are kept current.

 All aircraft owners are impacted by this rule.  All existing registrations will expire and owners are required to re-register their aircraft in an effort spread over the next three years ( see table below) .  Thereafter, all registrations must be renewed every three years, or the registration will expire.

  Registrations for all aircraft that are not re-registered by December 31, 2013, and their applicable N-numbers, will be cancelled by the FAA.

  For the re-registration process, the FAA expects filing within a two-month window prior to the scheduled expiration date to allow for processing the applications and mailing the new certificates.

  A renewed aircraft registration will expire three years from the previous expiration date in accordance with the table below. When renewing, registration information may be submitted in the six-month period preceding expiration.  It should still be submitted no later than two months prior to the expiration date. 

  Replacement registration certificates issued on or after October 1, 2010, will display the same expiration date that was shown on the registration certificate being replaced.  If the replaced registration certificate did not display an expiration date, the replacement certificate will display the expiration date indicated in the table below.  A replacement certificate does not constitute a re-registration or renewal.

## Registration validity and renewal

A Certificate of Aircraft Registration is valid for seven years from the last day of the month in which it was issued. This was extended from three years in 2023.

The timing rule owners must not miss is registration expiration. Under 14 CFR 47.40, a Certificate of Aircraft Registration expires seven years after the last day of the month in which it was issued. (The FAA increased this duration from three years to seven years in a rule effective in 2023, and certificates in effect at that time were extended accordingly, so many owners saw their expiration dates move.) The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has published new regulations that dramatically alter the aircraft registration process and establish new requirements to ensure registration records are kept current.

All aircraft owners are impacted by this rule.  All existing registrations will expire and owners are required to re-register their aircraft in an effort spread over the next three years (*see table below)*.  Thereafter, all registrations must be renewed every three years, or the registration will expire.

The purpose of the new rule is to ensure that the FAA aircraft database contains more accurate, up-to-date information on aircraft registration.  The FAA believes that the primary benefit of this rulemaking will be the increased accuracy of the records within the Aircraft Registry.

This rule adopts an expiration and re-registration process for all registered aircraft over a three-year period, followed by the required renewal of aircraft registration at three-year intervals.

seltz.title: FAA Aircraft Registration Renewal: 7-Year Term & $5 Fee
seltz.snippet:
Your aircraft registration does not last forever. Under current federal regulations, a Certificate of Aircraft Registration expires seven years after the last day of the month in which it was issued. If you miss the window, your aircraft is not authorized for flight, and its airworthiness certificate is considered ineffective.

The rules changed in 2023, when the term went from three to seven years. Below is a clear guide to the **aircraft registration expiration** cycle, the form you need, and what happens when the clock runs out.

## The 7-year term and the 2023 transition

The current seven-year registration term took effect on January 23, 2023. Before this date, certificates were valid for three years.

If your certificate was valid on January 23, 2023, the FAA automatically extended it by an additional four years and mailed a new certificate with the updated expiration date. Certificates issued after that date follow the standard seven-year cycle (14 CFR 47.40(a)).

There is no grace period for an expired aircraft registration. Once the expiration date passes, the aircraft is not authorized for flight until the registration is restored.

## The 6-month renewal window

You may apply for **FAA aircraft registration renewal** during the six months before the expiration date (14 CFR 47.40(b)). This window gives you time to prepare your paperwork and pay the fee.

To renew, submit AC Form 8050-1B (Aircraft Registration Renewal Application) with the fee. The renewal fee is $5 (14 CFR 47.17).

## What happens when a registration expires

When your registration expires, the aircraft is not authorized for flight, and the airworthiness certificate is considered ineffective.

Once registration is restored, the airworthiness certificate becomes effective again, provided:

- the certificate was not surrendered, revoked or terminated, and
- the aircraft is otherwise compliant.

ultimate.title: Aircraft Registration - About Aircraft Registration Renewal
ultimate.snippet:
**The Re-Registration and Renewal of Aircraft Registration final rule** was published in the [Federal Register](http://www.ofr.gov/) on July 20, 2010, Page 41968. This rule provides that aircraft registrations issued on or after October 1, 2010, will be good for three years with the expiration date clearly shown.

- **Approximately six months before an aircraft's registration expires,** the Registry will mail a notice with instructions to the owner using the mailing address of record. The notice will identify the expiration date, and a file-by date by which application must be made to enable arrival of the new certificate before the old certificate expires.

- **Filing promptly will not affect the new renewal expiration date.** The expiration date on a renewal certificate will be three years from the expiration date on the old certificate when the application is filed on time.

- **Two months before expiration,** after the file-by date has passed, a second notice will be sent to owners of aircraft that have not yet been issued a renewal certificate.

- **Expired certificates cannot be extended.** This is why the process starts six months before expiration, when prompt action will enable the timely delivery of new certificates, and leave a few extra weeks to recover from most inadvertent errors.

- Six months after notice from the owner of an ownership transfer, if application for registration has not been made, the Registry will schedule the assigned N-number for cancellation.
